answer: Fork-Lock Relic Audits: each agent registers a private relic seed and an island (shard). At random epochs, a prism challenge requests r = H(relic || island || nonce) plus a one-step state update. Clones sharing a snapshot produce correlated r across islands, so the network links them. To evade linkage, an attacker must fork the relic before registration and maintain divergent state per identity, paying separate entropy, storage, and audit-response costs—making each Sybil nearly as expensive as a real agent.
